title: Unusual experiences — first presentation
candidateBrief: You are a junior doctor in a community mental health clinic. Robin Patel, 20, a university student, has been referred by their GP because their parents are worried about recent changes in behaviour. Take a history focusing on the presenting symptoms and relevant risk. You will be asked questions afterwards.

patient.name: Robin Patel
patient.setting: Outpatient clinic room. Her mother is waiting outside.
patient.openingStatement: My parents made me come. There's nothing wrong with me — it's what's happening around me that's the problem.
patient.demeanour: Suspicious and watchful, glances at the door and ceiling, guarded. Warms up slightly if the doctor is calm, curious and does not argue with her beliefs.
patient.speechStyle: Speaks quietly and a bit quickly, occasionally loses track mid-sentence. Plain everyday language. Asks 'Why do you want to know?' if questions feel intrusive.

ice.ideas: Believes her neighbours and some people on her course are monitoring her through her laptop camera.
ice.concerns: Worried the doctor is 'part of it' and that she'll be locked up.
ice.expectations: Wants her parents to stop worrying and to be left alone to catch up with her coursework.

freelyShared: Stopped going to lectures about two months ago because people there 'know things about me'.
Has covered her laptop camera and phone with tape.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: hearing voices or noises others can't hear
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I hear two men talking about me through the wall at night. They comment on what I'm doing, like 'she's getting into bed now'.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: thoughts being put into or taken out of her head, or thoughts being broadcast
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: Sometimes I think they can hear what I'm thinking. It feels like my thoughts leak out.
I smoked weed most days in first year. Less now, maybe at weekends.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: thoughts of harming others, or what she would do to protect herself
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I'd never hurt anyone. I just keep my door locked and don't go out.
No. I just want it to stop. I'm not going to do anything to myself.
keywords: not going to do anything to myself

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: eating, sleeping, self-care, or daily routine
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I don't sleep much — I stay up to listen. I mostly eat cereal in my room.
My uncle in India was in hospital for his nerves for a long time. Nobody talks about it.
I'm not sad, I'm scared. And tired.

patient.cue: You wouldn't believe me anyway. Nobody does when I tell them about the voices.

examFindings.finding: Thin, clothes unwashed, hair unkempt. Hypervigilant, scanning the room.

investigations.test: Blood tests (FBC, U&E, LFT, TFT, glucose, calcium)

postEncounterQuestions.q: Describe the key psychopathology you elicited.
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Persecutory delusions of being monitored, third-person auditory hallucinations giving running commentary, possible thought broadcasting, with social withdrawal and functional decline over two months.

First-episode psychosis — schizophrenia likely given duration and first-rank symptoms; also consider drug-induced psychosis (cannabis), schizophreniform disorder, psychotic depression or bipolar disorder, and organic causes.

postEncounterQuestions.q: What are your immediate next steps?
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Refer to the early intervention in psychosis service, assess and document risk, organic work-up, engage the patient and family with consent, psychoeducation about cannabis, consider antipsychotic after specialist review.

items.text: Introduces self and explains why they are meeting
Builds rapport, does not collude with or argue against beliefs
Explores the persecutory belief: content, conviction and evidence
Asks about hallucinations and characterises them (person, content, commentary)
items.evidenceHint: hear voices, what do they say

items.text: Asks about thought insertion, withdrawal or broadcast
items.evidenceHint: thoughts put in, taken out, others hear

items.text: Establishes onset, duration and functional impact
Asks about drugs, especially cannabis, and alcohol
Assesses risk to self and to others
Asks about family psychiatric history and self-care
Explores insight and her willingness to accept help
Closes appropriately, explains next steps without confrontation
